display.title: Episode 12: The Lost Letter, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: Practicing for the grand parade with Moshiach, a phone call about the Shema, and chapter 2 of "The Lost Letter": Reb Leibel's fortune slips away until the forgotten letter turns up.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi recalls the great marches of Jewish history: leaving Egypt through the sea, crossing the Jordan with Yehoshua, and going up to the Beis HaMikdash three times a year. Soon there will be one more grand parade, when Moshiach leads us out of exile, so the soldiers of Tzivos Hashem practice with their homemade drums. After a recap, a young club member leads the Shema and tells how he is getting friends to buy letters in the children's Sefer Torah. In chapter 2 of "The Lost Letter", messengers bring Reb Leibel news that a factory has burned down, then a forest, and then more; over ten years his whole fortune disappears, because he refused the Baal Shem Tov's blessing, which would have opened a channel for good. Forced to sell his furniture, he has a big cedar closet carried out, and there on the floor lies the sealed letter. A child phones in to ask why we say the Shema, and learns it is said morning and night and comes from Devarim 6:4. The mailbox has a family's thanks and two riddles, and the contest is announced again.
display.lesson: A blessing from a tzaddik opens a channel for good; never think you have no need of a bracha.
